newsitem.title: UK: North Sea holds firm, Brent sold at Feb +9 cts.
newsitem.headline: North Sea holds firm, Brent sold at Feb +9 cts.

text.p: North Sea crudes held firm on Tuesday and the value of Dated Brent closed the year at February +9 cents after a trade at that level cleared some uncertainty over two earlier widely divergent trades.

A cargo loading Jan 9-11 was sold by a major to an unknown buyer at a number that was an average of Monday's two reported trades. Traders earlier said there was an apparent attempt to benefit related swaps.
"A major definitely wants the quote lower while others want it higher," a trader said.
Tuesday's seller was the same European major who sold a Jan 8-10 Brent at Feb Brent +5 cents on Monday after another major sold a Jan 11-13 cargo at Feb Brent +15 cents.
Meanwhile, a U.S.-based trader recently clocked with a couple of cargoes offered Brent at Feb Brent +20 cents.
Feb Brent paper firmed notionally to $23.78 a barrel in line with stronger IPE futures after trading several times at $23.60 late in the U.S. on Monday.
Intermonth spreads were broadly steady with Jan/Feb ending the session at +34/+38 cents and Feb/Mar at +56/+60 cents.
Traders said other North Sea grades were very quiet.
On Brent CFDs, the balance of this week was bid at +12 cents and the Jan 6-10/Jan 13-17 roll was talked at +12 cents, up from +8 cents earlier. A Jan 8-15 CFD was traded at Feb +12 cents.
No Brent cargoes were expected to turn wet on Tuesday, Shell UK having cancelled its Jan 15-17 equity cargo and Elf having moved its cargo forward to the Jan 14-16 loading period.

In the Mediterranean, Russian Urals was on offer after the port of Novorossiisk reopened briefly on Monday, allowing two crude tankers to sail. The port shut again at 2240 local time but was expected to reopen later on Tuesday, shipping sources said.
